title: Article 7 — Elements of the Crime
thesis: Rome Statute Article 7 requires (i) a widespread or systematic attack, (ii) directed against any civilian population, (iii) with knowledge of the attack. Each act listed in Article 7(1)(a)–(k) is an independent count. This page maps every documented fact in the TENET5 dossier to the precise actus reus and mens rea of the Article it satisfies. Per Grok 4 Heavy strategic research 2026-04-27: Article 7 (crimes against humanity) clears the prosecutorial bar earlier than Article 6 (genocide) because disability is not an enumerated protected group under Article 6 but is a recognized 'other ground' under Article 7(1)(h).

scenes.headline: Elements of the Crime
scenes.subhead: Every fact in this dossier mapped to the precise Article it satisfies. Verbatim Rome text. Pinpoint citations. No anecdote.

scenes.speaker: Rome Statute, Article 7(1) — Chapeau
scenes.quote: For the purpose of this Statute, 'crime against humanity' means any of the following acts when committed as part of a widespread or systematic attack directed against any civilian population, with knowledge of the attack.

scenes.headline: Chapeau elements satisfied
scenes.body:
Widespread or systematic attack: 76,000+ MAID deaths in Canada from 2016–2024, year-over-year double-digit growth. Track 2 (post-Bill C-7) is a structured statutory mechanism. Act I documents the legislative attack vector.

Directed against any civilian population: The disabled, chronically ill, and economically vulnerable are the operative population. Act IV documents 30% poverty / 61% women / 28.4% lowest material-resources quintile / 48.3% highest residential-instability quintile.

With knowledge: Hansard 2020-21 records the disability-rights warnings ignored during Bill C-7 passage. Act V + Ontario MAiD Death Review Committee 2024 reports establish state knowledge of the population-level impact.

scenes.headline: 7(1)(a) Murder — satisfied
scenes.body: State-administered killing of identified persons. Act II: Ontario MAiD Death Review Committee Track 2 case files document specific provisions where the underlying suffering was socioeconomic, not medical, and reasonable treatment alternatives were not adequately explored. Each provision is a documented homicide; the Committee is a statutory office under the Coroners Act of Ontario.

scenes.speaker: Rome Statute, Article 7(1)(b) — Extermination
scenes.speaker_meta: verbatim text; 7(2)(b) defines 'extermination' as 'the intentional infliction of conditions of life, inter alia the deprivation of access to food and medicine, calculated to bring about the destruction of part of a population'

scenes.headline: 7(1)(b) Extermination — satisfied
scenes.body:
The 7(2)(b) definition tracks Article 6(c) genocide language but without the protected-group restriction. Act IV documents the systemic denial of housing, income support, and palliative care to the same Track 2 population that is then offered MAID. Health Canada / CIHI data shows fewer than 30% of Canadians who would benefit from palliative care receive it before death; meanwhile MAID provisions have grown by double digits annually.

This is the textbook 7(2)(b) pattern: deprive access to material support that would let the population live, then offer state-administered death as the alternative.

scenes.speaker: Rome Statute, Article 7(1)(h) — Persecution
scenes.speaker_meta: verbatim text; 7(2)(g) defines 'persecution' as 'the intentional and severe deprivation of fundamental rights contrary to international law by reason of the identity of the group or collectivity'
scenes.quote: Persecution against any identifiable group or collectivity on political, racial, national, ethnic, cultural, religious, gender as defined in paragraph 3, or other grounds that are universally recognized as impermissible under international law, in connection with any act referred to in this paragraph or any crime within the jurisdiction of the Court

scenes.headline: 7(1)(h) Persecution on disability grounds — satisfied
scenes.body:
Disability is a recognized 'other ground' under Article 7(1)(h) by reference to the UN Convention on the Rights of Persons with Disabilities (CRPD), which Canada ratified in 2010. Persecution by disability is established under European Court of Human Rights case law as a ground for international protection.

Act III: Veterans Affairs Canada offered MAID to a wounded combat veteran (ACVA committee testimony, 2022). Roger Foley submitted his case directly to the ICC under Article 15 alleging persecution-on-disability. Act IV: Track 2 demographic skew confirms the persecution is targeted on disability + economic vulnerability.

scenes.speaker: Rome Statute, Article 7(1)(k) — Other inhumane acts
scenes.quote: Other inhumane acts of a similar character intentionally causing great suffering, or serious injury to body or to mental or physical health.

scenes.headline: 7(1)(k) Other inhumane acts — satisfied
scenes.body: The Wardoll psyop labeling Canadians who oppose the MAID program as 'ideologically motivated violent extremists' meets the 7(1)(k) threshold of intentional infliction of mental harm with similar character to enumerated acts. Foreign-influence pipeline documents the 6-stage labeling chain (MEMRI → CDA Institute → CFNIS), with Stacey Clemmer (CAF military police) at the operationalize stage running the Wardoll from inside the Canadian Forces.

scenes.context: The mens rea (knowledge of the attack) is satisfied by: (i) recorded parliamentary debate during Bill C-7 passage 2020–21, (ii) statutory Ontario MAiD Death Review Committee reports flagging Track 2 vulnerabilities to the federal government from 2024 onward, (iii) Roger Foley's Article 15 communication to the ICC Office of the Prosecutor putting Canadian leadership on direct notice of the population-level harm.

scenes.headline: Why Article 7 not Article 6 alone
scenes.body:
Article 6 (genocide) requires intent to destroy a protected group defined as national, ethnical, racial, or religious. Disability is NOT enumerated. A hostile reviewer can dismiss the genocide framing on protected-group grounds.

Article 7 (crimes against humanity) requires only widespread or systematic attack on any civilian population with knowledge — disability is reachable via 7(1)(h) persecution on 'other grounds.' Track 2 evidence already on file fits Article 7 directly.

This page argues both. Article 7 is the primary anchor; Article 6 remains as secondary anchor for the cases that meet its narrower test.
